subject.title: Bug: exec() tool strips dollar-variable patterns via undocumented template substitution

question: Should Windows exec support literal PowerShell expansion syntax after explicit one-shot approval, or should OpenClaw document direct `$...` PowerShell payloads as unsupported and steer users to script files or safer env/argv patterns?
rationale: Current main deliberately rejects expansion-like `$...` syntax in the Windows approval analyzer, while the issue expects command fidelity; the permanent choice changes approval UX, auto-review behavior, and the security boundary for Windows shell execution.

options.title: Sponsor One-Shot Approval
options.body: Review and prove the open PR’s approach where `$...` commands can reach explicit one-shot approval without auto-review or reusable allow-always trust.

options.title: Document Unsupported Payloads
options.body: Keep expansion syntax blocked in approval analysis and document script-file, env, or argv patterns as the supported Windows workflow.

options.title: Wait For Live Repro First
options.body: Keep the issue open without product direction until a maintainer can reproduce the exact Windows Gateway behavior on current main.

recommendation.title: Sponsor One-Shot Approval
recommendation.body: Review and prove the open PR’s approach where `$...` commands can reach explicit one-shot approval without auto-review or reusable allow-always trust.

likelyOwner.reason: Steipete is tied to the Windows PowerShell invocation history and is the strongest available routing candidate for a product/security boundary decision on this shell contract.
